A man not attyred.''] It profiteth not much to be within the Church and to be a Catholike, except a man be of good life, for {{ls}}uch an one {{ls}}hal be damned, becau{{ls}}e with faith he hath not good workes: as is euident by the example of this man, who was within, and at the fea{{ls}}t as the re{{ls}}t, but lacked the garment of charitie and good workes. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Church cō{{ls}}i{{ls}}teth of good and bad.}}And by this man are repre{{ls}}ented al the bad that are called. and therfore they al{{ls}}o are in the Church, as this man was at the fea{{ls}}t: but becau{{ls}}e he was called, and yet none of the elect, it is euident that the Church doth not con{{ls}}i{{ls}}t of the elect only. contrarie to our Aduer{{ls}}aries.

''21. To Cæ{{ls}}ar.''] Temporal duties and payments exacted by worldly Princes mu{{ls}}t be payed, {{ls}}o that God be not defrauded of his more {{ls}}oueraine dutie. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Neither mu{{ls}}t temporal Princes exact, nor their Subiects giue vnto them, Eccle{{ls}}ia{{ls}}tical iuri{{ls}}diction.}}And therfore Princes haue to take heede, how they exact: and others, how they geue to Cæ{{ls}}ar, that is, to their Prince, the things that are dewe to God, that is, to his Eccle{{ls}}ia{{ls}}tical mini{{ls}}ters. Wherevpon S. Athana{{ls}}ius reciteth the{{ls}}e goodly wordes out of an epi{{ls}}tle of the ancient and famous Cōfe{{ls}}{{ls}}or Ho{{ls}}ius Corduben{{ls}}is to Cō{{ls}}tantius the Arian Emperour: Cea{{ls}}e I be{{ls}}eche thee, and remember that thou art mortal, feare the day of iudgement, intermedle not with Eccle{{ls}}ia{{ls}}tical matters, neither doe thou commaund vs in this kinde, but rather learne them of vs. to thee God hath committed the Empire, to vs he hath cōmitted the things that belong to the Church: and as he that with malicious eies carpeth thine Empire, gaine{{ls}}ayeth the ordinance of God: {{ls}}o doe thou al{{ls}}o beware, le{{ls}}t in drawing vnto thee Eccle{{ls}}ia{{ls}}tical matters, thou be made guilty of a great crime. It is written, Geue ye the things that are Cæ{{ls}}ars, to Cæ{{ls}}ar: and the things that are Gods, to God. Therfore neither is it lawful for vs in earth to hold the Empire, neither ha{{ls}}t thou (O Emperour) power ouer incen{{ls}}e and {{ls}}acred things. ''Athan. Ep. ad Solit. vitam agentes''. And S. Ambro{{ls}}e to Valentinian the Emperour (who by the il coun{{ls}}el of his mother Iu{{ls}}tina an Arian, required of S. Ambro{{ls}}e to haue one Church in Millan deputed to the Arian Heretikes) {{ls}}aith: We pay that which is Cæ{{ls}}ars, to Cæ{{ls}}ar: and that which is Gods, to God. Tribute is Cæ{{ls}}ars, it is not denied: the Church is Gods, it may not verely be yelded to Cæ{{ls}}ar: becau{{ls}}e the Temple of God can not be Cæ{{ls}}ars right. Which no man can deny but it is {{ls}}poken with the honour of the Emperour. for what is more honorable then that the Emperour be {{ls}}aid to be the {{ls}}onne of the Church? For a good Emperour is within the Church, not aboue the Church. ''Ambr. lib. 5. Epi{{ls}}t. Orat. de Ba{{ls}}il. trad''.

''30. As Angels.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Saints heare our prayers.}}As Chri{{ls}}t proueth here, that in heauen they neither marry nor are married, becau{{ls}}e there they {{ls}}hal be as Angels: by the very {{ls}}ame rea{{ls}}on, is proued, that Saints may heare our prayers and helpe vs, be they neere or farre of, becau{{ls}}e the Angels do {{ls}}o, and in euery moment are pre{{ls}}ent vvhere they li{{ls}}t, and neede not to be neere vs, when they heare or helpe vs.

''30. As Angels.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Religious {{ls}}ingle life, Angelical.}}Not to marry nor be married, is to be like to Angels: therfore is the {{ls}}tate of Religious men and women and Prie{{ls}}ts, for not marrying, worthely called of the Fathers, an Angelical life. ''Cyp. lib. 2. de di{{ls}}cipl. & hab. Virg. {{ls}}ub finem''.

''32. Of the dead.''] S. Hierom by this place di{{ls}}proueth the Heretike Vigilantius, and in him the{{ls}}e of our time, which to dimini{{ls}}h the honour of Saincts, call them of purpo{{ls}}e, dead men.

''40. On the{{ls}}e two.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Not onely faith.}}Hereby it is euident that al dependeth not vpon faith only, but much more vpon charitie (though faith be the fir{{ls}}t) which is the loue of God and of our neighbour, which is the {{ls}}umme of al the law and the Prophetes: becau{{ls}}e he that hath this double charitie expre{{ls}}sed here by the{{ls}}e two principal commaundemēts, fulfilleth and accompli{{ls}}heth al that is commaunded in the Law and the Prophetes.
